Anton Chekhov, Three Sisters, translated by Julius West.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anton-chekhov/three-sisters/julius-west

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Anton Chekhov, the author, died 1904 (Wikidata Q5685, P570 = 1904-07-02).
- Julius West, the annotator and the translator, died 1918 (Wikidata Q19370740, P570 = 1918-01-01).

First publication of the text used: 1916 (SE colophon: 'Three Sisters was published in 1900 by Anton Chekhov. It was translated from Russian in 1916 by Julius West.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1916, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the country of first publication does not change this result. Every person named above died in 1918 or earlier, so the text is in the public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Three Sisters was published in 1900 by Anton Chekhov. It was translated from Russian in 1916 by Julius West.'
- Wikidata Q5685 (Anton Chekhov), P570 = 1904-07-02 (the facts also list 1904-07-15)
